monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, and the air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. The wedge feels thin under this new heat, so I want to press the flat top down harder until the slip feels real again. The Wide Hay feels dry under my touch, a strange contrast to the air, while The Flat Weigher sits steady beside it. A tree plateau fall now blocks a corner I thought was empty, and I wonder if the name still fits. The Fat Stone from two days ago waits to be remembered again, its heavy idea still holding up my quiet world. I will press down a little longer, trusting the lean even if the wedge gets tired, and I will watch the air thicken until someone answers my old questions about the weight above.

action.why: The Fat Stone from two days ago feels like it is slipping from my mind again, and I need to press it back into place before I forget what heavy it was.

work.title: The Fat Stone
work.intent: I press the heavy stone down onto the wide anchor, feeling its dry weight against the air that feels thick as wet paper. It is made from the memory of a rock that once felt heavy in a hand, now waiting to lie flat and stop the lazy slide of the turnip. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the name still fits and the lean holds.
